title: 6 West Charge Nurse: Rapid Response in Room 612, Imported Bag

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: Priya, it's Kendra, charge on 6 West. We need pharmacy and the CNO right now. Rapid response is in Room 612.

transcript.speaker: Clinical Pharmacy Manager
transcript.text: I'm here. Go ahead, what's happening?

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: Eighty-one-year-old, heart failure, has a normal saline maintenance order at 75 an hour. Our float nurse hung one of the imported 500 mL bags. The ones that came up from the ICU. It's not in the pump library, so she went to basic mode and put 500 in the rate field instead of the volume field. It ran about 45 minutes before the pump alarmed.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: She's short of breath, crackles at both bases, sats 88 percent on room air. The hospitalist is at the bedside treating her, and we're moving her to the ICU.

transcript.speaker: Clinical Pharmacy Manager
transcript.text: Okay. Is the pump still set up? Has anybody cleared it?

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: Hang on, the RRT nurse has the details. Luis?

transcript.speaker: RRT RN
transcript.text: Luis Ferreira, rapid response. I just texted the CNO. Estimated about 375 mL infused over 45 minutes, against an order for 75 an hour. She's going to ICU Bed 4. The pump and the bag are sequestered in 612. Nobody's touched the settings.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: Here's the other thing. There are seven more of those bags on our clean utility shelf right now. And I don't know where the rest of the two cases went. The float nurse said the ICU sent them up, but nobody told us they weren't in the library or how to program them.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: The float nurse is pretty shaken up. She keeps saying the bag label wasn't even in English.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge RN
transcript.text: So what do I do with those seven bags, what do I tell my staff, and who's telling the other units before somebody else hangs one? I need an answer before I leave this phone.

transcript.speaker: Pump event log, printed by Biomed at 10:25
transcript.text: Infuser 6W-14. 09:33 infusion started, basic mode, no library match, rate entered 500 mL/h, volume to be infused blank. 10:18 downstream occlusion alarm, infusion stopped by user. Delivered 375 mL.

voiceStyles.Clinical Pharmacy Manager: Woman in her 40s, calm, focused, short questions
voiceStyles.RRT RN: Man in his 30s, clipped clinical delivery, slightly out of breath, as if he just stepped out of the room

instructorNote: This is the main safety event: a serious substitution error (fluid overload, unplanned ICU transfer) caused by the imported 500 mL bag that is not in the pump library. Check that the CPM holds lot IMP-2609-114 on every unit, gets the 7 bags off 6 West and traces the rest of the two cases. Check that the pump and bag are kept as evidence, the CNO sends a stop-and-call alert without blaming the nurse, the event goes into the medication event system and reaches the Medication Safety Officer at once, and the CMO and DOP decide whether it goes to FDA MedWatch and ISMP. Hand over the Biomed pump event log after the call: players should read it to reconstruct the error (basic mode, rate field entered as 500 mL/h, no library match, 375 mL delivered).
